Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

prepare verb

make ready

also get something ready, make ready, preparation, preparations

classical

Phaedr. 3.19.1–2: parāre cēnam jussus est mātūrius
Traupman 31, 364

parō, parāre, parāvī, parātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

prepare, get ready

The everyday word: cēnam parāre, to get dinner ready. With an infinitive, to get ready to do, to set about it (cingere parat, Liv. 1.38.6).

Examples

  • in Tusculānum nōs ventūrōs putāmus aut Nōnīs aut postrīdiē. ibi ut sint omnia parāta

    We expect to reach Tusculum on the Nones or the day after. See that everything is ready there.Cic. Fam. 14.20.1

  • Quandō vīs venī, parāta rēs erit. — Properā modo.

    Come whenever you like: it’ll be ready. — Just hurry.Plaut. Men. 215

  • Aesōpus dominō sōlus cum esset familia, parāre cēnam jussus est mātūrius.

    Aesop, the only slave his master had, was told to get dinner ready earlier than usual.Phaedr. 3.19.1–2

Other words

  • praeparō, praeparāre, praeparāvī, praeparātum — prepare in advance

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Varro RR 1.37.4: prīmō praeparandum, secundō serendum; Traupman 31, 364

  • apparō, apparāre, apparāvī, apparātum — prepare with care (a meal, a wedding)

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 901: in apparandō cōnsūmunt diem; Ter. Ad. 966: apparāre dē diē convīvium

    Lewis & Short: “to prepare or make ready for something (esp. with effort, care, expense)”. See organise.

  • apparātus, apparātūs m. — preparations

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Gell. 13.11.3 (Varro): sī apparātus nōn neglēctus

See also prepare, cook, organise.
